claim:coupled-fate-oscillator.proposition: Two sub-cellular simulators of different formalisms — an SBML-ODE metabolism and a MaBoSS Boolean fate network — can be coupled inside one cell in both directions (the ODE's metabolite C pins the fate 'high_C' input, mode A; the fate 'divide' output resets the metabolism, mode C) to produce a metabolism↔fate feedback oscillator that neither formalism exhibits alone.

claim:coupled-particle-catalysis.proposition: A Smoldyn particle simulator and an SBML-ODE can be coupled inside one cell so that the particle population drives the ODE's kinetics (mode B): the live count of a particle species sets the ODE's rate constant each step, so the ODE product accumulates faster as the particle population builds — a cross-formalism catalysis no single engine expresses.

claim:coupled-triple-cell.proposition: A single cell can run all three sub-cellular formalisms at once — a Smoldyn particle sim, an SBML-ODE metabolism and a MaBoSS fate network — coupled by all three modes simultaneously: the particle count catalyses the metabolism (B), the metabolite pins the fate input (A), and the fate output resets the metabolism (C).

claim:fateful-tissue.proposition: Every scale this workspace can simulate composes into one system: a tyssue of dividing cells, each running a Smoldyn particle sim confined to its moving polygon (split on division) AND an ODE metabolism whose metabolite pins a MaBoSS fate network — and the fate 'divide' output DRIVES the tissue division. Cells grow as they metabolise (target area tracks the metabolite), divide when their own fate fires, and daughters reset and regrow, so the tissue sustains. Biology decides when the tissue divides.

claim:bounded-particles-cpm.proposition: A Smoldyn particle sim composed with the cpm backend keeps every cell's molecules strictly inside that cell's moving boundary (voxel-region outlines traced from the occupancy), conserves molecule count when a cell divides (each molecule inherited by exactly one daughter, by containment), and lets the reversible reaction A+B<->C reach equilibrium inside the living tissue.
evidence_refs: particles bounded by cpm cells — flipbook

claim:bounded-particles-vertex.proposition: A Smoldyn particle sim composed with the vertex backend keeps every cell's molecules strictly inside that cell's moving boundary (junction-tension polygons), conserves molecule count when a cell divides (each molecule inherited by exactly one daughter, by containment), and lets the reversible reaction A+B<->C reach equilibrium inside the living tissue.
evidence_refs: particles bounded by vertex cells — flipbook

claim:bounded-particles-munk.proposition: A Smoldyn particle sim composed with the munk backend keeps every cell's molecules strictly inside that cell's moving boundary (pymunk discs (oblong under crowding)), conserves molecule count when a cell divides (each molecule inherited by exactly one daughter, by containment), and lets the reversible reaction A+B<->C reach equilibrium inside the living tissue.

claim:scene-model-mixed-formalism.proposition: A declarative scene (cells + types) bound to a per-type model registry compiles to one composite in which metabolic cells run an SBML-style ODE, signalling cells run Smoldyn particles and fate cells run a MaBoSS Boolean network, all coupled to a shared extracellular field through typed membrane transport.

narrative.question: This workspace has three tissue-scale simulators (Cellular Potts, vertex, center-based) and three sub-cellular simulators (SBML-ODE, Smoldyn particles, MaBoSS Boolean). How many genuinely different models can we build by COMPOSING them — coupling sub-cellular simulators to each other inside one cell, coupling sub-cellular to tissue, and coupling all scales at once — and what does each composition let us model that no single simulator can alone?
